name: Building permit expiry, progress and renewal rules by jurisdiction
description: How long a building permit stays valid, what keeps it alive, what it costs to renew once it has lapsed, and how the local rule differs from the model-code section it amends. One record is one rule for one jurisdiction, placed next to the adopted code section it replaces. Answers 'how long is a building permit valid before it expires', 'does an inspection reset the permit clock', 'my building permit expired what do I do', 'building permit renewal fee after expiration', and 'IRC 105.5 permit expiration'. The memorised answer is 180 days and it is wrong in the places people ask about: unincorporated San Diego County allows two years to start work, then requires a passed inspection every 180 days, with an outer life of three years and renewal at one-half of current permit fees — one-quarter if only a final inspection remains. DC's adopted code gives one year to begin, with a 180-day carve-out for residential work and no more than four extensions per permit.
licence: Facts extracted from freely published municipal and county building department pages and from published jurisdiction-amended code sections, with a short attributed quote and a link back. Expiry periods and renewal fee bases are facts about a legal requirement, not reproductions of a standards developer's expression. UpCodes is used only for the amended-section value with a short attributed quote, never as a bulk source: its product IS the compilation of code text and it is in active litigation with ICC and ASTM over exactly that. Prefer the jurisdiction's own publication wherever it exists.

records.commencement_deadline: it will expire if the work is not started within two years. To meet this requirement, the permittee must call for, and pass a valid inspection
records.inactivity_window: passing a valid inspection at least every 180 days (six months)
records.maximum_life: all work must be completed within three years
records.renewal_fee_basis: One-half of current permit fees are due upon renewal unless progress has been made (and approved) so that only a final inspection is needed, then one-quarter of current permit fees are due
records.source_quote: San Diego County's Building Code sets timeline requirements when building permits are issued. The work authorized by the permit must begin and demonstrate progress by certain dates, and all work must be completed within three years. From the day the permit is issued, it will expire if the work is not started within two years. To meet this requirement, the permittee must call for, and pass a valid inspection. If no inspection has been scheduled and passed within the first two years, the permit becomes null and void. Once the work has started and the first required inspection has been passed, the permittee must show that the work is progressing by passing a valid inspection at least every 180 days (six months). If these progress requirements are not met the permit will expire. This applies regardless of when the first inspection took place within the first two years of the life of the permit. To renew an expired building permit that has received and passed at least one valid inspection, but has not exceeded the three-year mark: The plans cannot be changed, nor changes proposed. One-half of current permit fees are due upon renewal unless progress has been made (and approved) so that only a final inspection is needed, then one-quarter of current permit fees are due. records.extension_rule: extensions of time not to exceed 180 days per extension. Not more than four extensions of time will be granted to any permit. The code official may issue an extension for a period of 365 days upon demonstration of need at the time of extension application, but, in no event, shall the aggregate extensions of time exceed two years
records.source_quote: 105.5.1 Extension of Permit A <https://up.codes/viewer/district-of-columbia/ibc-2012/chapter/2/definitions#permit_> permit may be extended upon written request, prior to expiration and upon a showing of good cause. The code official is authorized to grant extensions of time not to exceed 180 days per extension. Not more than four extensions of time will be granted to any <https://up.codes/viewer/district-of-columbia/ibc-2012/chapter/2/definitions#permit_> permit . The code official may issue an extension for a period of 365 days upon demonstration of need at the time of extension application, but, in no event, shall the aggregate extensions of time exceed two years.
